title: Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful
hook: the Most Merciful, whose mercy covers everything that exists

segments.voice: Yesterday, Allah, the name itself, with no plural and ending in a breath. Your line was the name of names.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions are camped at Hudaybiyyah, outside Mecca, and a peace treaty is being written with the Quraysh, the people who drove them out. Ali holds the pen. The Prophet dictates the first words: bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. And the Meccan envoy, Suhayl, stops him. As for ar-Rahman, he says, by God, I don't know what that is. Write in Your name, O Allah, the way you used to. The companions bristle. It's the first line of the treaty, and it's already a fight. What happens next says something about the name itself.
screen: `A TREATY AT HUDAYBIYYAH.` → `ALI HOLDS THE PEN.` → `I DON'T KNOW WHAT AR-RAHMAN IS.`

segments.voice: The Prophet said: write it as he asks. Bismika Allahumma. In Your name, O Allah. Bukhari records it. The name of mercy gave way so that peace could be written, and some readers see mercy itself in that. Why didn't Suhayl know the name? The report doesn't say, but the Qur'an records Meccans asking the same thing: and what is ar-Rahman? It comes from r-h-m, the root of mercy, and its form, fa'lan, is one that grammarians say Arabic uses for things that are full, overflowing, at their peak, like ghadban, full of anger, or 'atshan, full of thirst. So ar-Rahman is mercy at its fullest. Scholars say the name belongs to Allah alone; no person is to be called ar-Rahman. And the Qur'an gives it an entire surah. Surah ar-Rahman opens with the name alone, then lists gifts: the Qur'an taught, speech, the sun and moon in their courses, fruit, the palm with its sheaths, grain, the two seas. Thirty-one times it asks, which of the favors of your Lord will you deny? In Surah al-A'raf, in Pickthall's translation: and My mercy embraceth all things. One classical explanation reads ar-Rahman as mercy that reaches every creature in this world, whoever they are, whatever they believe: the rain falls on every field. The name's closer partner comes tomorrow.
screen: `WRITE IT AS HE ASKS.` · `WHAT IS AR-RAHMAN?` · `FA'LAN — FULL, OVERFLOWING.` · `MY MERCY EMBRACETH ALL THINGS.` · then, large: `MERCY COVERS ALL.`

segments.voice: With your eyes softly open, look for mercy for one minute, not the dramatic kind: the light through a window, the chair holding you up, the air arriving in your lungs without being asked, your heart doing its work while you weren't paying attention. Name each one silently as you find it, then close your eyes and let the list keep going on its own. If you pray, you can say, ya Rahman, softly, at the end.
Ar-Rahman. The Most Merciful, mercy at its fullest, overflowing onto everything that exists, a name used only for Allah. Today's word.
Your line: mercy covers all. Like the rain, it falls on every field, even the ones you'd pass by. That's day two hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Muslims say ar-Rahman in every bismillah, and Surah ar-Rahman, with its refrain about the favors of the Lord, is often recited; Abdul-Rahman, servant of the Most Merciful, is a common name.

chat.says: What makes the name ar-Rahman special?
options: It's mercy at its fullest, overflowing on everything, and used only for God.
It means the Just Judge, the name used when deeds are weighed.
It's a title any very kind person may be called out of respect.
chat.meaning: Its form means full, overflowing; ar-Rahman is mercy at its fullest, and scholars say no person is called by it.
